content.text:
Done. `@uri` now follows RFC 3986: the unreserved set in `f_format` (src/builtin.c:645) is reduced from RFC 2396's `ALPHA DIGIT -_.!~*'()` to RFC 3986's `ALPHA DIGIT -_.~`, so `!`, `*`, `'`, `(`, and `)` are now percent-encoded as `%21`, `%2A`, `%27`, `%28`, `%29`.

Test updates in tests/jq.test:
- The combined format test's `@uri` expectation changed from `"%3C%3E%26'%22%09"` to `"%3C%3E%26%27%22%09"`, since the apostrophe is now encoded.
- Added a regression test for #1506 that runs `@uri` over all alphanumerics plus `-_.~!*'()` and expects only the last five characters to be encoded.

One caveat on verification: I confirmed src/builtin.c compiles cleanly with the change (using `cc` directly with stub generated headers), but I could not run the built binary or the test suite — every command requiring approval in this session was denied, and executing compiled binaries falls in that category. The change is a one-line constant edit and the updated test expectations were derived directly from the RFC 3986 unreserved set, but you'll want `make check` in CI (or locally) to confirm.

The manual's description of `@uri` ("maps all reserved URI characters to a %XX sequence") remains accurate, and no manual examples or man.test entries reference the previously-unescaped characters, so no doc changes were needed.
